reason: The cited evidence (E1) discusses oxide formation and stability on a different material (high-temperature alloy) under dry sliding wear, not corrosion of Q235 steel in saltwater mist. It does not address surface defects as nucleation sites, the effect of polishing, or passivation film uniformity, leaving all key premises unsupported by specific prior evidence.
premises: Surface defects act as nucleation sites for corrosive oxide formation on Q235 steel.
Polishing reduces surface defect density on Q235 steel.
Reducing nucleation sites delays corrosion onset and slows corrosion rate.
Elevated temperature accelerates oxidation kinetics, amplifying the effect of defect minimization.
Polished surfaces form more uniform, protective passivation films than untreated surfaces.
